extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3, 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, with pages hand-picked to minimize binarized images and prioritize tables, forms, lists, and figures. Questions and answers were collected using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Minimized binarized images; prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over running text; OCR tokens extracted using a commercial OCR application.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process. Stage 1: Remote workers defined up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, entering answers verbatim. Stage 2: Verification where different workers answered the questions and assigned question types, flagging inapt questions. Stage 3: Author review of mismatched answers from stages 1 and 2, with editing or rejection.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Disagreement analysis involved comparing answers from Stage 1 and Stage 2. Mismatches were sent to a third review stage where authors decided to accept (with edits) or ignore the question.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; Authors; Volunteers from the institution
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Names of people, institutions, and places
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset is biased towards documents from the food and nutrition collections (due to image quality), the 1960-2000 time period, and the tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical industries.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Large performance gap compared to human performance. Models struggle with questions requiring understanding of document structure. OCR errors can impact results.
